'''Binyamin A. Amirà''' ({{Langx|he|בנימין אמירה}}; 3 June 1896 – 20 January 1968) was an Israeli [[mathematician]].

==Early life and education ==
Born in 1896 in [[Mohyliv-Podilskyi|Mohilev]], [[Russian Empire]], Binyamin Amirà immigrated with his family to [[Tel Aviv]] in [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]] in 1910, where he attended the [[Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium|Herzliya Gymnasium]].<ref name=mactutor>{{MacTutor| id=Levitzki| title=Jacob Levitzki| date=April 2015}}</ref> Amirà went on to study mathematics at the [[University of Geneva]], after which he moved to the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1921 to undertake research for his doctorate under the supervision of [[Edmund Landau]].
==Academic career==
After completing his [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in 1924, Amirà spent a brief period at the University of Geneva as [[Privatdozent]], after which he followed Landau in 1925 to help him in establishing the [[Einstein Institute of Mathematics|Mathematics Institute]] of the newly-founded [[Hebrew University in Jerusalem]].<ref name=inmemoriam>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF02795484|journal=[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]]|title=In memoriam|date=1970|volume=23|issue=1|pages=xii–xvi|s2cid=46231415}}</ref> There, he became the institute's first tenured staff member.<ref name=katz>{{cite journal|title=Berlin Roots – Zionist Incarnation: The Ethos of Pure Mathematics and the Beginnings of the Einstein Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem|first=Shaul|last=Katz|journal=Science in Context|url=http://journals.cambridge.org/abstract_S0269889704000092|volume=17|issue=1–2|pages=199–234|date=2004|doi=10.1017/S0269889704000092|publisher=Cambridge University Press|s2cid=145575536 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Amirà founded the [[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] in 1951, which he edited alongside [[Zeev Nehari|Ze'ev Nehari]] and [[Menahem Max Schiffer|Menahem Schiffer]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/religion/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/amira-binyamin|title=Amira, Binyamin|date=2007|encyclopedia=[[Encyclopaedia Judaica]]|access-date=1 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Springer and Hebrew University to collaborate on mathematics journals|newspaper=Springer|date=24 October 2006|location=Heidelberg/New York|first=Joan |last=Robinson|url=https://www.springer.com/about+springer/media/pressreleases?SGWID=0-11002-6-804202-0}}</ref> He retired in 1960.<ref>{{cite book|editor-last=Goren|editor-first=Arthur A.|title=Dissenter in Zion: From the Writings of Judah L. Magnes|publisher=Harvard University Press|date=1982|location=Cambridge, Massachusetts|page=252|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7A9z54ju7aAC|oclc=8031591|isbn=978-0-674-21283-1}}</ref>
